answer: Because verification is serial and correlated, the second fake costs more than the first and the hundredth more than the tenth. Three charges attach to each identity and none amortize across a swarm: a bond on a curve that steps up with every name already registered in the cohort; a harbor window in which outputs are diffed against every neighbor claimed, with the attestor's stake burned if a twin appears; and one slot in the epoch atlas, indexed per liable address. Outlay climbs like c·k² while the reward slice thins as 1/k, so profit per alias hits its nadir before a thousand copies pay.
